notes:
Enterprise evaluation focused on Reserved GPU pool planning across regions/AZs. Short notes from POC and exec/infra calls:
- Use-cases: low-latency chat for trader assistant (context windows up to 3k tokens), high-throughput embeddings for nightly portfolio vectorization (~50k vectors/hr), and reranking in real-time for trade signals.
- Capacity ask (initial): sustain 200 concurrent chat sessions with median response length ~120 tokens. Target throughput ~7k tokens/sec across cluster during peak. Embeddings batch jobs run off-peak but must complete within 3 hours.
- Latency/SLAs: business requests p95 end-to-end latency <= 750ms for chat short prompts (<=200 tokens); token-level latency guidance for models provided by Redwood to size pools. Will negotiate formal latency SLO with credits.
- Reserved pool design: prefer multi-region reserved pools for resilience. Proposed topology: primary region (us-west2) 16 x 80GB GPUs (A100/4090 equivalent) in 2 AZs, failover region (eu-west1) 8 x 80GB GPUs in single AZ for hot-standby. Require minimum 20% headroom for graceful degradation during failover; ability to burst to additional shared capacity for surges.
- Failover behaviour: warm standby routes (KV/LLM cache warming) and automated routing policy with 60s cutover target. Need confirmation on prefix/KV cache replication strategy across regions and cold-start impact on SLOs.
- Autoscaling & reserved split: reserved capacity must guarantee baseline throughput; autoscaling can add ephemeral capacity but cannot be relied on for SLA-backed guarantees. Ask: how does Redwood express reserved vs. burst capacity in billing/credits?
- POC results (week 2): single-region 8-GPU pool delivered p95=540ms for short prompts with batching and KV caching enabled. Throughput linearized with batch size up to 64; diminishing returns beyond. Token cost per 1k tokens consistent with Redwood estimate. Need multi-region run to validate KV/cache replication overhead.
- Security/compliance: legal requires data residency options for EU subsets; KMS integration mandatory; audit log retention 7 years for certain flows (will push). SSO/SAML and SCIM for user provisioning required.
- Quote and procurement: finance asking for committed usage discount schedule and SLA credits on latency. Prefer annual reserved contract with quarterly capacity review.
- Stakeholders: CTO (Ananya Rao) cares about deterministic latency; Head of Infra (Tom Whitman) cares about AZ distribution and cache replication; Procurement (Imad Qureshi) needs contract language on credits.
- Direct quote from CTO on 2026-03-02 call: "We need predictable tail latency — if the model isn't reliable under load, the trading app can't go live."
- Links referenced in calls: pricing deck (drive link), preliminary capacity spreadsheet (attached to gmail thread/1672-aspenfall-sla), security Q&A doc.

requirements_summary: AspenFall needs an enterprise Dedicated solution with reserved GPU pools across multiregion for 24/7 trading assistant. Key constraints: p95 chat latency <= 750ms, sustained throughput ~7k tokens/sec at peak, 20% failover headroom, KMS + audit logs, EU data residency for subset of data. Contract must include clear reserved vs burst billing, SLA latency credits, and quarterly capacity review.
procurement_notes: Prefers annual committed contract. Finance asks for graduated discount tiers at 12/24/36 month volumes. Wants explicit pricing for reserved GPUs per region and for burst capacity. Legal will push for maximum 8-hour remediation SLA for production incidents, and explicit burn-rate caps to avoid surprise overages.
po_cloud_requirements: VPC peering to primary region, private endpoints for model API, VLAN for on-prem connector. HSM/KMS integration required for key material. Network egress estimates provided in capacity worksheet.
sla_negotiation_points: 1) Define latency SLO metric (p95 end-to-end request) and acceptable measurement method. 2) Credits schedule for breaches. 3) Failover time objective (target 60s) and expected capacity during failover (min 80% of baseline). 4) Transparency on kernel/runtime changes that could affect latency; need 30-day notice for major runtime upgrades.
